headline: Endangered species are running out of time—their populations too small to sustain
universal_truth: Critical thresholds exist; decline can accelerate past a point of no return; intervene before it's too late
fun_facts: Tigers have declined 97% in the last century—fewer than 4,000 remain wild
The vaquita porpoise is down to about 10 individuals—functionally extinct
Some species have recovered from near-extinction: American bison went from 325 to 500,000
discussion_questions: What in your life is 'endangered'—declining toward extinction?
When do you intervene versus accept loss?
What relationships or skills are you neglecting to the point of danger?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: The last male northern white rhino died in 2018. Fewer than 10 vaquita porpoises remain. These species crossed a threshold—too few individuals to sustain the population. They're running out of time. Some things can't be recovered once lost.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Endangered species decline gradually, then suddenly. Small populations become vulnerable to collapse. What does this pattern teach us?

options.text: Decline has tipping points—gradual loss eventually crosses thresholds that trigger accelerating collapse; intervention must happen before critical thresholds
options.response: Yes. Small populations become inbreeding-prone, disease-vulnerable, catastrophe-susceptible. Decline feeds on itself. The lesson: address problems while recovery is still possible.

options.text: Some species just aren't fit for modern conditions
options.response: Fitness matters, but human changes happen faster than evolution—species can't adapt quickly enough...

q1.title: Minimum Viable Population
q1.script: Species need minimum populations to sustain—genetic diversity, breeding opportunities, catastrophe resilience. Below these thresholds, extinction becomes likely even without further harm.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Minimum Viable Population"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Accelerating Decline
q2.script: Small populations decline faster. Fewer mates, less genetic diversity, more vulnerability to disease and disaster. Decline accelerates past certain points. Early intervention matters.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Extinction Risks
q3.script: You have 'endangered species' in your life too—relationships you're neglecting, skills you're not using, health you're degrading. Decline that crosses thresholds becomes hard to reverse.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Critical thresholds exist. Decline can accelerate past a point of no return. Intervene while recovery is still possible.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 268. Tomorrow, we'll explore places species call home—habitats. Until then, identify what in your life might be endangered.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Endangerment Audit - What's At Risk?
growTrack.activity: What in your life is declining—a relationship, a skill, your health, a dream? Is it approaching a critical threshold? What intervention could reverse the decline while recovery is still possible? Address it before it becomes endangered.
